Semiclassical and high-temperature approximations are both determined and contrasted to their respective classical or quadratic behaviors. Furthermore, the canonical thermal equilibrium states are found to correspond to specific ellipsoidal regions in the space of symplectic matrices. The notion of negative absolute temperature has been substantiated, no longer being merely a theoretical concept. Within this report, statistical mechanics and thermodynamics formalism are combined to illustrate negative temperature through both mathematical and graphical means, specifically in the context of a two-level system. We contend that the simplicity of these calculations can offer undergraduates a clear, tangible understanding of the concept of negative absolute temperature. Furthermore, we highlight the implications of negative absolute temperature on the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and the second law of thermodynamics, demonstrating its observed violation to be actually a result of preconceived notions rather than the negativeness of temperature itself. Instead, we find that the violation arises from the conditions of its application, yielding insights into the distinct characteristics of negative absolute temperature and its distinction from apparent violations of the second law of thermodynamics. We also examine the relationship between negative absolute temperature and the appearance of negative values of the average energy and the heat capacity. Ultimately, our discussion equip students with a comprehensive, intuitive grasp of negative absolute temperature, its underlying causes, and its sometimes misleading effects on physical phenomena. We demonstrate that the concept of negative absolute temperature is neither enigmatic nor ennobling, but rather a concrete, accessible idea with a rich history. We also explore the possible sources of confusion that have led to the lasting myth surrounding negative absolute temperature, embracing an opportunity to set the record straight. We hope that our report will contribute to a deeper understanding of this concept, relieving both students and seasoned physicists of any existing apprehension. We anticipate that the combined statistical mechanics and thermodynamics formalism used in our analysis will also serve as a valuable resource for undergraduate students seeking a clearer, more intuitive grasp of the underlying physics. We employ exact diagonalization to examine the effects of spin-orbit coupling and electron-electron interactions on the mixing of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ $d$-orbital states in a cubic crystal structure, characteristic of transition metal oxides. By directly comparing with $t_{2g}$ only or $e_g$ only models based on electron filling, we investigate the magnetic properties of all possible $d$-shell configurations, incorporating calculations of the total magnetic moment, orbital occupation, and effective spin-orbit coupling. The resulting parameters are expressed in terms of interaction strength, spin-orbit coupling, and crystal field splitting within relevant 4d and 5d transition metal oxide ranges. Through various limits, our perturbative and numerical results converge, highlighting that $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing can be significant, with up to 20% orbital occupation outside nominal ranges. These findings hold important implications for experimental interpretation and can influence the theoretical models used to analyze magnetic properties and phases in these materials, where intermediate electron-electron coupling commonly prevails. Furthermore, our approach provides a framework for evaluating the effectiveness of mean-field theories in these complex, mixed-orbital systems. The widespread presence of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing across these materials suggests a new paradigm, challenging traditional orbital-based categorizations and encouraging a wider consideration of its effects in the field. The knowledge gained from this study can be extended to other transition metal compounds featuring competing energy scales and intricate electronic configurations. The need for a nuanced understanding of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals is further emphasized by the frequent coexistence of all $d$-shell configurations in solid-state chemistry and physics, where the interplay of shape, size, and electron-electron interaction influences the complexity of intrinsic phenomena and defect behaviors. The results presented here are relevant to various materials including Sr$_2$IrO$_4$, Ba$_2$IrO$_4$, Ru, Os, and Ag-doped Ti, with the approach and findings offering broader implications for the theoretical modeling of transition metal oxides. Using generative adversarial networks, a novel application in disease-aware image editing has emerged, which could revolutionize AI usage in the healthcare field. In this research, a concept for GAN-based medical imaging enhancement is demonstrated. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. By incorporating an encoder from the Cyclic Reverse Generator framework, we successfully developed an inverse mapping system to recreate synthetic X-rays accurately and reconstruct organs on real X-rays. By fine-tuning latent codes, we successfully transplanted a cardiac enlargement condition onto normal chest X-rays. ViDaExpert is an application for multidimensional data visualization and
advanced analysis. It is capable of handling object-feature tables that include
numerical values and text-based labels for objects and features. The tool
encompasses several statistical techniques such as weighted PCA, elastic maps,
linear discriminant analysis, and decision tree construction, in addition to
K-Means clustering and multilinear regression. With customizable visualizations
and an interactive 3D viewer, ViDaExpert enables the creation of 3D scenes
from data and facilitates rapid, in-depth analysis of data, encompassing
elementary to complex methodologies. The application is particularly suited for
experiments in cognitive science and neuroscience, where often vast amounts
of data need to be examined following stimulation by human subjects. The guide
covers setup, data import, 3D visualization, and exemplary studies. The
approach described herein provides a framework for extending ViDaExpert to other
domains and areas of research. The source code of ViDaExpert is available at
https://github.com/Neurocognitivo/ViDaExpert. The application and example
sessions can be accessed from the project website at
https://neurocognitivo.github.io/ViDaExpert/. The code and applications are
released under the MIT license, and the published work is available at
